similarities.point: Both identify helots as a subjugated population in Spartan-controlled Laconia.
similarities.quote_britannica: the inhabitants of Helon, a town of Lacom, conquer by the Spartan
similarities.quote_wikipedia: a subjugated group that constituted a majority of the population of Laconia

similarities.point: Both state that helots were conquered and made prisoners by Sparta.

similarities.point: Both describe helots as performing labor to support Spartan citizens.

similarities.quote_wikipedia: Tied to the land, they primarily worked in agriculture as a majority and economically supported the Spartan citizens

differences.point: Britannica locates helots at a single town called Helon, while Wikipedia discusses Laconia and Messenia broadly.

differences.quote_wikipedia: constituted a majority of the population of Laconia and Messenia

differences.point: Britannica says Spartan women were barred from manual or mechanical work, a claim absent from Wikipedia.
differences.quote_britannica: The femme of Sparta were forbidden the excerite of any mean on mechanical employment
differences.quote_wikipedia: Tied to the land, they primarily worked in agriculture as a majority and economically supported the Spartan citizens

differences.point: Britannica presents helot origins as a simple conquest of one town, whereas Wikipedia details multiple contested origin theories.
differences.quote_britannica: the inhabitants of Helon, a town of Lacom, conquer by the Spartan
differences.quote_wikipedia: Several theories exist regarding the origin of the name "helot"

differences.point: Britannica omits the helots' eventual liberation, which Wikipedia describes.
